venue.name: BC Forest Discovery Centre
venue.description: The BC Forest Discovery Centre is a 100 acre open air museum in Duncan with a working narrow gauge railway. The site has forest and marsh trails, a 1930s logging camp with bunkhouses, a 1905 schoolhouse, antique logging equipment and an indoor exhibit hall. School programs on forest heritage, forest ecology and Indigenous stone tools are offered in the spring and autumn, and each one includes a train ride. Groups of ten or more can also pre book a group admission rate with a guided tour included.

facility_notes.washrooms: Wheelchair accessible portable toilets are on-site whenever the museum is open to the public.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Many of our visitors bring a picnic lunch to enjoy a pleasant break in the picnic area on our lower grounds during their visit. Visitors may leave and re-enter the site.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Most main areas of the site are wheelchair accessible, including the main entrance and exhibit hall, the gas and steam trains, antique vehicle building, most heritage buildings, and the main walking trails. A few of the heritage buildings as well as the speeder are not wheel chair accessible at this time.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Designated parking stalls are available for people with mobility disabilities.

restrictions: Only Certified Guide & Service dogs are permitted in our food service areas and on board our trains.
Group rates do not apply for the Halloween Train or the Christmas Express
venue.hours_notes: Open Thursday to Monday, 10:00 am to 4:30 pm, and closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. In spring and early autumn the gas train runs every hour from 11:00 am with the last train at 4:00 pm. In summer the train runs every half hour from 11:00 am with the last train at 3:30 pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: The regular season runs from early April to 20 September 2026. Evening Halloween and Christmas train events run in October, November and December. School programs on forest heritage and forest ecology run in May, June and September, and the Christmas program runs in December.
venue.price_year_or_season: General admission prices are the 2026 season rates. The group booking rates on their tours page are still dated 2025 and may have gone up.

programs.name: Forest Heritage: Fallers, Flunkies & Families
programs.description: A guided visit to the heritage logging camp for younger classes, focused on what camp community life was like in the early to mid twentieth century. The program includes a ride on the narrow gauge train and access to the picnic area, playground, exhibits, heritage buildings and forest trails. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Walk around the old logging camp, go inside the bunkhouses, the 1905 schoolhouse, the Westholme Post Office and the blacksmith shop, and hear how the people who lived there worked. Then ride the train for about twenty minutes right around the property and over the trestle, with a ten minute stop at the lower grounds.
programs.our_note: This one runs outdoors and goes ahead in rain, so pack for weather. There is a playground and a picnic area, so it is easy to add lunch and stay on after the ninety minutes are up.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are portable toilets on site, and lunch is an outdoor picnic area on the lower grounds. Bus parking and how many adults have to come are not published, so ask when you book.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.

programs.name: Forest Heritage: Springboards & Swedish Fiddles
programs.description: A guided logging camp program for older classes, focused on the technology and transport used in logging camps and communities in the early to mid twentieth century, including the slang the loggers used. The program includes a train ride and access to the rest of the site. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Look at the tools and machines the loggers used, learn the camp slang for everyday things, and go through the bunkhouses and other camp buildings with a guide. Then ride the train around the property and over the trestle.
programs.our_note: The camp lingo is the hook here, so it lands well with a class that likes words and puzzles. It is outdoor walking on gravel and grass for most of the ninety minutes.
programs.practical_summary: Portable washrooms and an outdoor picnic area are on site, and the main routes are step free. Bus parking, indoor shelter in bad weather and how many adults have to come are not published.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.

programs.name: Forest Ecology: Eagles & Ecosystems
programs.description: A guided walk through the mature second growth forest for younger classes, looking at the plants and animals of the forest ecosystem and ending at the bald eagles' nest. Children are introduced to local plants and trees with their Hul'q'umi'num' names and uses. The program includes a train ride. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Walk a gentle loop through forest with 400 year old Douglas fir, cedar, alder and big leaf maple, stop to look up at the eagles' nest, and learn the Hul'q'umi'num' names for some of the plants along the way. Then ride the train around the property.
programs.our_note: It is a real walk on forest trails, so put the children in shoes that can get muddy. The eagles are not always in residence, so treat seeing them as a bonus rather than the point of the trip.
programs.practical_summary: Portable washrooms and an outdoor picnic area are on site, and the main trails are step free. There is no published wet weather fallback, and programs go ahead rain or shine.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.

programs.name: Forest Ecology: Timber Stamps & Tree Rings
programs.description: A guided forest walk for older classes covering tree parts and functions, forest recycling, forest technology and how trees are used as a resource, ending with a walk to the eagles' nest. The program includes a train ride. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the mature forest with a guide, look closely at tree rings, timber stamps and how a forest recycles itself, and carry on to the eagles' nest. Then ride the train around the property and over the trestle.
programs.our_note: This is the version to ask for if the class has already done a basic forest walk. It goes further into how forestry actually works rather than just naming trees.
programs.practical_summary: Portable washrooms and an outdoor picnic area are on site, and the main trails are step free. Bus parking and how many adults have to come are not published, so it is worth a call.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.
programs.evidence: Timber Stamps & Tree Rings Ages 9 - 12 / Grades 4 - 6

programs.name: Stone Tool Collection: Indigenous Artifacts Program
programs.description: An interactive program built around the Marsh Collection, a set of Indigenous stone tools gathered on this site between 1951 and 1964, when it was the Cowichan Tribes S'amunu Village and later Somenos Lake Farm. Students compare the artifacts, work out what they were used for and discuss who used them. The centre says the program meets the Grade 3 Social Studies learning standards. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Hold and turn over real stone tools, sort out which ones look alike and work out what each was for, then take a short walk to see the ground where they were found.
programs.our_note: Children get to handle the actual objects, which is unusual and is what makes this one stick. It is written to the Grade 3 social studies standards, so a younger or older class may need it adjusted when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Portable washrooms and an outdoor picnic area are on site. Whether this program runs indoors in poor weather is not published, so ask when you book.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.
programs.evidence: The Marsh Collection: Indigenous Artifacts Program meets the Ministry of Education prescribed learning standards for Grade 3 Social Studies.

programs.name: O' Christmas Tree
programs.description: A December program in the historic 1905 schoolhouse about how the Christmas tree has changed over time, from candles to LED lights and from homemade ornaments to glass balls. Each child makes an ornament to take home and the group rides the decorated Christmas Train. The centre says it meets Social Studies and Science learning outcomes for kindergarten to grade 3 and can be customised for high school special needs classes. Price is per student and GST is added on top.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the old wooden schoolhouse among historically decorated trees, make a Christmas tree ornament to take home, and then ride the decorated Christmas train.
programs.our_note: This is the one that works for the youngest classes, because most of it happens sitting down indoors with something to make. It only runs in December and books up against the evening Christmas Express events, so ask early.
programs.practical_summary: Most of this program is indoors in the schoolhouse, with portable washrooms and an outdoor picnic area on site. Bus parking and how many adults have to come are not published.
programs.extra_fees_note: Includes education program and train ride
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.
programs.evidence: Oh Christmas Tree Ages 5 - 8 / Kindergarten - Grade 3

programs.name: Group visit with guided tour
programs.description: Groups of ten or more paying visitors can pre book a group admission rate, which includes a guided tour where one is available. The choices are the Camp Life Tour at 30 minutes, the Foresters Walk at 45 minutes and the Stone Tool Collection Tour at 45 minutes, each followed by the 2.5 km train ride around the property. The rates recorded here are the shoulder season group rates published for 2025, so check them before you budget. Group rates do not apply to the Halloween Train or the Christmas Express.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide around the logging camp, the forest trails or the stone tool collection depending on which tour you choose, then board the train for a twenty minute ride around the 100 acres and over the trestle, with a ten minute stop at the lower grounds. Afterwards the group can wander the exhibits, the heritage buildings and the playground.
programs.our_note: This is the route to take if your group is mixed ages or too big for a school program. Check the price before you commit, because the rates on their groups page still carry 2025 dates while the general admission page has moved on to 2026.
programs.practical_summary: Portable washrooms, an outdoor picnic area and step free access to most of the site, including the trains. Bus parking is not published and there is no stated wet weather fallback, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children 2 and under Free. Youth 13 to 18 years are $14.00 at the shoulder season group rate.
programs.payment_timing: Please arrange for payment in advance or upon arrival
programs.cancellation_note: There is a 48 hour cancellation policy.
programs.evidence: Groups of 10 or more paying customers can pre-book to receive the BC Forest Discovery Centre group admission rate.

images.alt: A long dark red wooden building with FOREST DISCOVERY CENTRE painted along the front, seen from above, with a paved car park and tall evergreens behind it.
A guide in a blue jacket and cap stands on a gravel path in the forest talking to a group of adults, with ferns and bare branches around them.
An empty wheelchair strapped onto a metal lift platform beside a railway carriage, with a person in denim overalls standing next to it.
A steam locomotive pulling a line of cars across a tall wooden trestle bridge over still water, in a dark toned photograph.

gaps: How many adults have to come with a class is not published anywhere on the site, and neither is whether accompanying adults get in free on a school program. Ask when you book.
The group rates on their groups page are dated April to September 2025 while the general admission page has been updated to 2026. Treat the group prices as out of date and confirm them.
No minimum notice for booking a school program is published, so there is no way to tell how far ahead you need to ask.
Which days of the week school programs run on is not published. The centre itself is closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
There is no published wet weather fallback. Programs commence rain or shine, and most of the site is outdoors.
Bus parking is not mentioned. The site only says there are designated stalls for people with mobility disabilities.
Washrooms on site are wheelchair accessible portable toilets. There is no mention of a change table or of indoor washrooms.
The site says programs are also available for preschool groups but gives no age range, price or length for them.
Their contact page gives the address as North Cowichan and their directions page gives it as Duncan. The street number and postal code are the same on both.
The brochure is dated by its file path to June 2025, so its prices may be a season old even though it is the current link from their tours page.
Whether programs are sensory friendly, quiet or suited to neurodiverse groups is not addressed, beyond a note that programs can be customised for special needs classes.
The Christmas program photo on the tours page had no alt text and was not opened, so it is not recorded here.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: this site fetches fine without a browser. A browser was used to re-read the group and admission prices from the live page and to look at the photographs before writing descriptions of them.

conflicts.note: Their web page and their printed program brochure give two different email addresses for the same education coordinator. If one bounces, try the other, or ring the office. We use the one from their tours page.

Their brochure splits the forest programs into two tight grade bands while their web page says the same programs suit kindergarten right up to grade seven. If your class sits outside the narrow bands, say so when you book and ask whether they will adapt it.

Their brochure says school programs run in May, June and September, while their web page says they run right through the season from Easter to Thanksgiving. Ask for the month you want and see what they say.
